summary: A 45–52 minute customer-facing interview recorded for a short podcast/case-study. Aurora HealthTech discussed their migration to Redwood Inference for in-app clinical note summarization and patient triage models. Key themes: latency/cost wins, security and data residency needs (VPC + KMS), and measurable uptick in user engagement. Marketing will produce a 10–12 minute highlight reel and publish a written case study.
topics: intro/permissions, background on Aurora use cases, technical migration story, performance outcomes (latency/cost), security/compliance discussion, customer impact stories, marketing next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, welcome — quick check, this is being recorded for a short customer spotlight, is that all good on your side?
[00:05] Lena: Yep, we're good. Thanks for having us.
[00:08] Maya: Awesome. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Jordan is our SE, and Talia from marketing is dropping in to capture notes.
[00:16] Jordan: hey! great to meet you all.
[00:18] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Samir and Alex with me.
[00:22] Dr. Samir: Morning.
[00:24] Alex: Hey team.
[00:27] Maya: Cool. So format — we'll have a conversational interview, we might pause for clarifying questions, and then Talia will recap. If anything's sensitive just flag it and we'll skip.
[00:35] Lena: sounds good. we have a short list of outcomes we can mention.
[00:38] [00:40] Jordan: maybe a quick high level — how long have you been using Redwood in prod?
[00:42] Lena: We went live in production January this year, so about 7 months, the feature is automated clinical note summarization and a triage classifier for inbound patient messages.
[00:51] Jordan: Nice. And before Redwood what was the stack?
[00:53] Lena: we were running on a managed endpoint from another provider plus some self-hosted LLMs on EC2 — it was... expensive and latency was all over the place. Also the KV cash kept getting invalidations — oh sorry, I mean KV cache. transcription mis-say.
[01:08] Dr. Samir: yeah, and we couldn't really get consistent tail latency at peak. Some requests spiked to multiple seconds.
[01:15] Alex: And for growth, that user-facing lag led to dropoff in message-thread completion.
[01:20] [01:24] Maya: Great, so what were the key criteria when you evaluated Redwood?
[01:27] Lena: predictability, lower unit cost, and enterprise security. We needed SSO, SAML, SOC 2 proofs, and we had to keep PHI in our VPC.
[01:35] Jordan: Short note — did you do the Dedicated offering or Redwood Private?
[01:37] Lena: We chose Redwood Dedicated initially — reserved pools with VPC peering and a KMS integration for key management. Private is on the roadmap for some highly regulated clients.
[01:47] [01:50] Dr. Samir: The setup was pretty straight forward, Redwood's SE team helped with the network peering and the KMS policies. There were some questions around audit logs and retention which Redwood addressed via the console export.
[02:05] Jordan: Happy to hear that — we tried to make the audit exports easier.
[02:08] [02:15] Maya: Can you share any metrics — latency, token cost, or user engagement changes you saw? This is great material for the case study.
[02:20] Alex: Sure. Post-migration our 95th percentile latency went from ~1.8s to ~380ms for the summarization path. Cost per 1k tokens dropped by about 42% after we enabled batching + mixed-quantization profiles. Engagement for message threading improved by ~12% in the first 30 days.
[02:41] Lena: and we saw fewer support tickets for timeouts which helped ops.
[02:45] [02:50] Jordan: That's a solid win. Do you have a preferred anonymized screenshot or metric you want us to use?
[02:56] Alex: we'll share a CSV and a slide — I'll put those in the shared drive link: https://rwd.shared/aurora/metrics (note: link is internal placeholder).
[03:08] [03:12] Maya: great. On the technical side, were there any gotchas during testing?
[03:15] Dr. Samir: mostly around quantization tradeoffs — some of our clinical prompts are sensitive to hallucinations. We worked with Jordan to pick a quantization/profile combo and a small rerank heuristic to keep precision up. At first we saw a tiny drop in F1 on one prompt set, but with tuned temperature and post-rerank the quality recovered.
[03:38] Jordan: yeah, we iterated through a couple of kernel selections and sequence-length batching policies, and then pinned a model variant for canary rollout.
[03:47] [03:54] Lena: The KV cache inconsistencies from our prior deploys were fully resolved with Redwood's prefix caching; that was huge.
[03:59] Maya: Nice. For compliance — any questions customers always ask that you'd want us to mention?
[04:03] Lena: People ask about data residency and audit trails. We had to demonstrate SAML SSO, role-based access, and KMS-managed keys. The SOC2 docs were helpful.
[04:15] [04:20] Jordan: Did you use the private data plane for any workloads?
[04:22] Lena: Not yet, but for a couple of enterprise prospects we showed how Private would work in a VPC/on-prem style deployment. That reassured them.
[04:31] [04:35] Talia: quick production story — any customer anecdote we can quote about the UX improvement?
[04:38] Alex: one of our care coordinators said, quote, 'we used to wait; now the summary is basically instantaneous — it's saved me a ton of time.' Feel free to shorten.
[04:50] Lena: Please anonymize patient details.
[04:53] Maya: Absolutely. We'll sanitize.
[04:56] [05:00] Jordan: Switching gears — marketing side, how would you like to be positioned?
[05:03] Alex: We're happy to be a partner story focusing on scale and security — nothing too product-specific.
[05:08] Lena: if you can highlight the latency and cost numbers that's golden.
[05:12] Talia: Noted. We'll produce a short 10-minute audio cut and a 700–900 word case study.
[05:19] [05:24] Maya: Any objections or competitors we should be aware of in the messaging?
[05:27] Dr. Samir: Some folks asked about Anthropic's endpoints during eval, but Anthropic's cost profile didn't match our traffic pattern. Also we looked at some open-source stacks with heavy infra maintenance.
[05:39] [05:44] Lena: the argument to buy was the operational lift savings and consistent SLAs.
[05:49] Alex: also consolidation — fewer vendors.
[05:52] [06:00] Maya: Okay, logistics — we'll send the draft transcript and audio for sign-off. Do you want a staged publish (blog first, then podcast) or simultaneous?
[06:08] Lena: staged — blog first, short audio clip after we sign quotes.
[06:12] Talia: We'll aim for publish week of 2025-08-25 pending approvals.
[06:17] [06:25] Alex: works for us.
[06:27] Lena: one question — can you include a short technical sidebar that we can review, like how batching works in Redwood?
[06:33] Jordan: yes we can draft that. We can include a small diagram on how prefix caching + batching reduces per-token cost.
[06:41] [06:45] Talia: Great. Any final micro-stories or quotes?
[06:48] Alex: Care coordinator quote above; also our ops lead said, 'rolling outages are less common' which you can paraphrase.
[06:56] Lena: that's it from us, thanks.
[06:59] Maya: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the editorial calendar and the assets list.
[07:05] Talia: Thanks, everyone.
[07:08] [07:10] End of recorded portion — quick unrecorded notes: we should capture the CSV and the anonymized screenshots.
[07:14] [Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings, 'KV cash' appears once; some proper nouns slightly off.]
